newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission tries to convince Council on film fund.
newsitem.headline: Commission tries to convince Council on film fund.

text.p: The European Commission has urged EU member states not to delay any further and to push forward with its proposal for an audiovisual guarantee fund to boost Europe's flagging film sector.

"The establishment of the new mechanism should not be delayed further," the Commission says in an internal document on the proposal, COM(95)546, that was made available to reporters and presented to member states on Thursday.

The Commission says in the document that an EU contribution of 90 million Ecus would have a lifespan of 17 years, time enough to set up a guarantee fund as a separate legal entity, the condition for incorporating outside capital.
Before the legal entity was set up it would work on the basis of EU contributions and with a system of agreements with outside partners.

"This model demonstrates that provided strict management criteria are applied, the fund will have a long lifespan. It may operate for 17 years without any new call having to be made on the community budget," the paper says.
To make the fund viable, only productions with a commercial potential which would allow them a cross-border career would be covered.
The Commission says that over a period of 10 years the fund would contribute to financing 415 cinema productions and 215 television productions -- namely 35 percent of European co-productions.
The European Film Companies Alliance urged adoption of the fund, saying in a statement that the film sector in the EU represents a potential of two million jobs over the next 10 years.
The European Parliament is expected to back the fund at its plenary session this month.
